# Review — bardo-thodol-005 (pp. 45–54)

## Pass 1

Checked against conventions.md, QUESTIONS.md, packet.md (the pinned print, its twelve `# fix:` lines and the establishment
log with the three readers' logs), units.py and bardo-thodol-001.json (pilot), the units of 002–004, 004's review.md and
glossary.json. All 49 units were read word by word, from the original to `l` to `i`, and every grammatical label in the
notes was checked against the form. Units are numbered here 1–49 in file order (the drafter's list of doubts numbers some
of them one lower). units.json was edited in place by script (ensure_ascii=False, indent 1, as the file was written; a
round-trip of the unedited file was checked to be byte-identical first). `w` is unchanged: no division was found wrong.
Letter check (all `w` joined with spaces, ' / ' removed, against `hooks.letters()` for the part): 49 units, 4748 letters,
PASS; verse line counts w / l / i equal (u. 11, 39: six lines each).

### Changes

- u. 6, 36 · n · minor · stem label. The note to u. 6 called ltung "the print's spelling here of lhung". ltung and lhung are stems of one verb "to fall": ltung is the present and future stem, lhung the past · u. 6 now says so, with "the sense is the same". u. 36 now calls lhung "the past stem, as on the second day (ltung above)".
- u. 17, 46 · n · minor · stem label. bod was called "the print's spelling here of 'bod … a known variant". bod is the future stem of 'bod ('bod / bos / bod / bos), a proper form, the same kind of case as blta in 004 · now says so; the same formula on the second and third days and on the fifth day (u. 46) has the present 'bod. u. 46 now says "the print has the present stem 'bod" in place of "writes 'bod with its first letter".
- u. 33 · n · minor · the variant was misreported: "the other recension has bros shig", which would be "flee!", the opposite command. The log (50.5) gives མ་བྲོས་ཤིག, the same sense · now "the other recension writes ma bros shig".
- u. 44 · l, n · minor · byon was labelled "'came'" and `l` had "came" while `i` and the parallel u. 45 ('ong ngo) have the present. byon, the respectful verb, has one form for every tense · `l` now "meeting for come"; the note "byon, 'to come', the respectful word …, with one form for every tense".
- u. 2 · n · minor · "'ong ba … stands for 'ongs pa, 'has come'" said the present form means the past one; the print simply has another form here, and `i` rightly translates it "coming" · now "stands where the days before had the past 'ongs pa, 'has come' (on the second day read from the print's yongs pa)".
- u. 21 · n · minor · Sanskrit names (drafter's doubt 6). གྷཱིརྟི was said to be "for Gītā" as a fact, though ghīrti is no Sanskrit word and the identification comes from the set of eight female bodhisattvas, not from the letters; ཨཱ་ལོ་ཀེ was glossed "she of the lamp", but āloka is "light" (the lamp is the goddess's emblem, not the word) · now: ghīrti "as it stands is no Sanskrit word … taken as a spelling of gīti, 'song', and so as Gītā … but the letters do not show it plainly"; ā lo ke "is āloke, the form of address of āloka, 'light', for Ālokā, 'she of light'" (as 004's pass 2 treated puṣpe).
- u. 21, 49 · l · style · `l` gave the bodhisattvas' and consort's names in Sanskrit ("Avalokita and Mañjuśrī", "Commitment-Tārā"), where 004 (u. 16, 40; u. 8, 15, 32) renders the Tibetan names word by word in `l` ("Earth's-Essence", "Sky's-Essence", "Buddha-Eye") and keeps Sanskrit for names written in Sanskrit letters (Lāsyā, Māmakī) · now "Eye-Looker and Gentle-Glory", "Commitment-Saviouress"; `i` keeps Avalokiteśvara, Mañjuśrī, Samayatārā.
- u. 22, 39, about · i · style · "the discriminating wisdom" for so sor rtogs pa'i ye shes: `l` has "discerning" and the note "the wisdom that discerns each thing", and "discriminating wisdom" is a stock phrase best not taken over · now "the discerning wisdom" (about: "his red discerning wisdom").
- about · style · "give up desire": the text bids him give up attachment and clinging (chags zhen, chags sems, u. 25, 37); desire is the poison that drives him · now "give up attachment".
- u. 35 · i · style · "That is the welcoming path of the hungry ghosts, gathered by fierce desire." left it unclear what is gathered, and broke from the rendering of the same formula in u. 5 and 004 u. 4, 28 ("the path on which … come out to meet you") · now "That is the path on which the hungry ghosts gathered by fierce desire come out to meet you." (bsags pa'i qualifies yi dwags, as the note says).
- u. 1 · l · style · "as-own-radiance": `l` puts fused endings after the word (004 u. 49 "own-radiance-as") · now "own-radiance-as".
- u. 37 · l · style · bkag pa'i was "blocking's" here and "blocked's" in u. 7 for the same past stem · now "blocked's".
- u. 5 · n · style · "As on the second day" did not say that bag chags is the first day's word in this place (the second day had sdig sgrib) · added.
- u. 27 · n · style · bskyed "the past of skyed": it is the past and future stem, as glossary.json has · now so.
- u. 11 · n · style · drafter's doubt 3. The reading of yi as yis is right, but the note gave only the sense as support · added that the print writes gi for gis elsewhere (gcig gi … tshar in the pilot; conventions.md lists it as a habit of the print).
- u. 16 · n · style · drafter's doubt 1. The kyis after 'od lam gnyis was not explained · added: it marks the two light-paths as what comes, as 'od lam gyis kyang in u. 45.
- u. 39 · n · style · drafter's doubt 4. "the print's spelling here of skyol" is right in substance, but bskyol should be shown not to be a stem in its own right · now "bskyol is none of the regular stems of skyel (skyel / bskyal / bskyal / skyol); it is read as the imperative skyol … the print's spelling"; bskyor named as in u. 11.
- u. 43 · n · style · drafter's doubt 7. "the dead go on down through the days" made mar la a descent; of time mar is "on, onward" · now "mar la, 'downward' (mar, 'down', the opposite of yar, 'up'); of time mar is 'on, onward' …". `l` "downward" and `i` "wander on down to the fifth day" kept.
- u. 49 · n · style · drafter's doubt 8. "the throne of the north is borne by them" was stated from the pictures, not the text, which says only shang shang gi khri · now "'the shang-shang throne', as the days before had lion, elephant, horse and peacock thrones".

Severity count: major 0 · minor 6 · style 13 (19 change lines).

### Drafter's doubts, adjudicated

1. u. 16 ཡི་དྭགས་ལ་འོད་ལམ་གཉིས་ཀྱིས: the reading stands. The la is clear on the image (log 48.1), the other recension has kyi, and the
   note says both; "with(?)" in `l` marks the doubt. 'od lam gnyis kyis is the subject, the two light-paths, as in u. 45; a
   line on this was added to the note. `i` "come to meet them as two light-paths" gives that sense and is kept.
2. u. 35 བསགས་པའི་ཡི་དྭགས་ཀྱི་བསུ་བའི་ལམ: the print's reading is translated as it stands (bsags pa'i qualifies yi dwags: the
   hungry-ghost birth that desire has heaped up), and the note gives the other recension's bag chags. Right. `i` was brought
   into the formula's form (above).
3. u. 11 མཱ་མ་ཀི་ཡི read as "by": right; `l` "of(by?)" shows the form, the note gives yis as the first day's word and the
   other recension's. Support from the print's gi-for-gis habit added.
4. u. 39 བསྐྱོལ called the print's spelling of སྐྱོལ: right; bskyol is no regular stem of skyel, and the log lists སྐྱོལ/བསྐྱོལ
   among the print's spellings. Wording sharpened (above).
5. u. 22 འདུ་ཤེས "perception" against 004's "notion": kept. 004 u. 21 and 003 u. 49 have 'du shes as an ordinary noun ("a
   notion of delight"); here it names the third aggregate, where "perception" is the plain English for saṃjñā, and the note
   says that it is the word rendered "notion" before. glossary.json gives both senses.
6. Sanskrit names: Sukhāvatī (bde ba can), Pāṇḍaravāsinī (gos dkar mo), Avalokiteśvara, Mañjuśrī, pratyavekṣaṇājñāna (so sor
   rtogs pa'i ye shes), Amoghasiddhi, Samayatārā (dam tshig sgrol ma), samaya, preta, kleśa, asura are right. Gītā and Ālokā
   are the usual names, but ghīrti is not gīti in its letters, and āloka is "light", not "lamp": the note now says so
   (above). Rab brtsegs pa is rightly given no Sanskrit name: the print's name differs from the other recension's, and no
   name is asserted for it.
7. u. 43 མར་ལ "downward": kept in `l`; the note refined (above).
8. u. 49 ནམ་མཁའ་ལྡིང་ ཤང་ཤང: the division (two words, the garuḍa's name and the reduplicated shang shang) is right, and `l`
   "Sky-soaring shang-shang's throne" follows the letters. nam mkha' lding may be read as a name in apposition ("the garuḍa
   shang-shang") or as a describing word; `i` takes the second, which the letters (nam mkha', "sky"; lding, "soar") give
   and the note explains. The iconographic claim was trimmed (above).
9. Metre (the verses, u. 11 and 39): every line has nine syllables (the first after kyai ma), in both prayers, the same as
   004 u. 8 and 32: nga rgyal / 'dod chags drag pos 'khor bar 'khyams pa'i tshe = 9; mnyam nyid / sor rtogs ye shes gsal ba'i
   'od lam la = 9; bcom ldan rin chen 'byung ldan / snang ba mtha' yas lam sna drongs = 9; yum mchog mA ma ki yi / gos dkar
   mo yis rgyab nas bskyor = 9; and 9 in the last two lines. read_A's remark (log 46.3–4) that the print's first line "has
   ten" and the other recension's 'khyams tshe "keeps nine" is a miscount: 'khyams tshe gives eight. Nothing to note in the
   unit, since the difference is not of sense.

### Findings considered and refused

- u. 42 · n "dngangs is the print's spelling of sngangs, as in 003": read_C calls དངངས "the ordinary spelling"; both spellings
  are found, the other recension has sngangs, and 003 u. 14 says the same as this note. Kept for agreement with 003.
- u. 22 · `i` "perception" for 'du shes: see doubt 5. Kept.
- u. 16 · `i` "come to meet them as two light-paths" for 'od lam gnyis kyis: rendering the subject "the two light-paths" with
  the host and the ghosts as their owners would follow the other recension's kyi, not the print's la. Kept.
- u. 23 · no mention that the print lacks the third day's khyod rang gi mdun du before snying gi thad kar: the log records no
  difference here, and the sense is the same. Kept.
- u. 26 · 'ongs, a past stem, rendered "will … flee" in `i`: the note explains that bros su 'ong(s) says what will happen, as
  in 004 u. 44; `l` shows "came". Kept.
- u. 11 · the other recension's 'khyams tshe at 46.3–4: a difference of metre, not of sense (doubt 9). Kept out of the note.
- u. 19 · `i` "peacock throne" for gdan, "seat": as 004's refused finding (u. 14, 38). Kept.
- u. 12, 40 · `i` "When he makes the prayer" while the unit addresses no one: the third person is 004's rendering of the same
  formula. Kept.
- u. 48 · rab brtsegs pa given no Sanskrit name: right; asserting the other recension's realm name (or its Sanskrit) would
  go beyond the print. Kept.
- u. 15 · bskyod given as "past of skyod" only (it is past and future): nothing false, and the past is what the sentence
  has. Kept.
- u. 30 · `i` "Dissolving inseparably, you will become a buddha" names no subject for thim: the note says that what
  dissolves is not named, and the print is followed. Kept.

the notes, and the master entries of related forms (stems, case and particle forms, parts, Sanskrit); then all 49 units read
again from the original through `l` to `i`, with the master entries of the 231 known forms read against how they are used
here. Both files were edited by script (ensure_ascii=False, indent 1; a round-trip of each unedited file was checked to be

or gloss.json, no gloss.json key is already in the master, none is unused, the key set equals novel-forms.json, every

' / ' removed, equals `hooks.letters()` for the part (4748 letters, PASS); hooks.assemble + hooks.validate with the merged
glossary report no error.

### Changes: gloss.json

- gloss བྲོས་བས · stem · minor · "because they flee (bros 'flee' …)": bros is the past of 'bros, and the entry gave no stem · now "because (they) fled, fleeing (bros, past of 'bros 'to flee', + -bas, …)".
- gloss བྲོས་ཅིག · stem · minor · "bros 'flee' + cig": the form is the imperative of 'bros, and cig after -s is the print's writing where the rule gives shig (the note to u. 33 gives the other recension's shig) · now says both.
- gloss ཨཱ་ལོ་ཀེ · Sanskrit · minor · "āloke, the address of āloka 'light'": the vocative of the masculine āloka is āloka (āloke is its locative); āloke is the form of address of the feminine name Ālokā · now "the form of address of the name Ālokā, from āloka 'light'"; the note to u. 21 likewise (below).
- __broaden__ ན · new · minor · the master has only "if, when; also 'in, at'"; in skye rga na 'chi (u. 6) na is "to be ill", as the note says · broadened with "to be ill, sickness (na, the verb of na ba)".
- __broaden__ བཞུགས་པ · new · minor · the master has "abiding, being present (bzhugs, respectful 'stay')"; here (u. 19, 49) gdan / khri la bzhugs pa is "seated on", as `l` and `i` have · broadened with the respectful "sit".
- __broaden__ པདྨ · new · minor · the master entry ends "Here the Lotus family …"; in u. 19 padma is the flower held in Amitābha's hand, and the entry as it stands would mislead · broadened with the flower as an emblem held in the hand.
- gloss བཀག་པའི · stem · style · "of blocking, that blocks" for a past stem (pass 1 made `l` "blocked's" in u. 7 and 37) · now "of what has blocked, that blocks".
- gloss བསྐྱོད · stem · style · "past of skyod": bskyod is the past and future stem; the gloss is general to the form (pass 1 rightly left the note to u. 15, which concerns the past) · now "past and future stem of skyod 'to move, to stir'".
- gloss ཞིང · grammar · style · "the form of zhing after ng" said nothing; zhing stands after a vowel and after ng, n, m, r, l, ' · now so, with cing, shing.
- gloss སྐྱེ · stem · style · now "the present and future stem; past skyes" (the master's སྐྱེས "past of skye").
- gloss རྒ · sense · style · only the noun; rga is first the verb "to grow old" · added.
- gloss ལ་སོགས་པ · parts · style · no parts · now la 'to' + sogs 'et cetera' + -pa, as the master's ལ་སོགས.
- gloss ཉམས་པ · parts · style · no parts · now nyams 'decline, be damaged' + -pa, as the master's ཉམས.
- gloss སྐལ་ཆད · stem · style · chad now "past of 'chad".
- gloss གོས་དཀར་མོ · parts · style · "dkar mo 'white', with the feminine -mo" · now "dkar 'white' + -mo, the feminine ending".
- gloss སྤྱན་རས་གཟིགས · parts · style · "ras gzigs 'looking'" gave ras a meaning it does not have (ras is "cloth"); gzigs is the respectful "look" · now spyan + ras + gzigs, with ras left unexplained.
- gloss གྷཱིརྟི་མ · parts · style · the -ma was not shown as a part · now "ghīrti, the print's letters, perhaps for gīti 'song', + -ma".
- gloss བྱོན་ནོ · sense · style · "the respectful 'come' used of a buddha": byon is the respectful "come, go" for any honoured being, and with one form for every tense the entry should not give the present only · now "comes, came … used of a buddha or other honoured being".
- gloss རབ་བརྩེགས་པའི · stem · style · brtsegs "stacked" · now "piled up, past of rtseg".
- gloss རྡོ་རྗེ་རྒྱ་གྲམ · Sanskrit · style · no Sanskrit, while the other emblems and names have it · now viśvavajra.
- gloss ནམ་མཁའ་ལྡིང · parts · style · no parts · now nam mkha' 'sky' + lding 'soar, hover'.
- gloss མར · sense · style · the form is also the common word "butter"; the entry is general to the form · added as "another word of the same spelling".
- __broaden__ ལ · wording · style · "among (skal chad kyi rigs la …)" copied the line of u. 14 · now "among (… kyi rigs la 'among those of the … kind')", "on (… la bzhugs 'seated on …')".
- __broaden__ གནས་སུ · wording · style · "(mi'i gnas su ltung …)" copied the line of u. 6 · now "(… gnas su ltung 'fall into the abode of …')".

### Checked and confirmed (no change)

- Stem claims left standing, each checked: ltung present and future, lhung past (as pass 1 put it in the notes to u. 6 and 36); bod future of 'bod ('bod / bos / bod / bos); 'ong ba present ('ong / 'ongs / 'ong); bkag past of 'gog ('gog / bkag / dgag / khog); bskyed past and future of skyed; bsags past of gsog; spong present in mi spong bar; zhog imperative of 'jog; bskyol read as skyol, imperative of skyel (skyel / bskyal / bskyal / skyol); bskyor past and future of skyor; byon one form for every tense.
- The print's -ba for -pa after -n and -s (yin ba'i, rtogs ba'i, bros bas, 'ong bas) named as its spelling in gloss and notes alike; zhing after ng (myong zhing), shing after s ('ongs shing), ste after ng ('byung ste, 'ong ste, myong ste), te after s ('jigs te, skyes te, 'khyams te, bcas te) covered by the master's ཏེ ("this print also writes it after other letters").
- "perhaps" kept where the notes call a reading uncertain: ཡི read as 'by' (u. 11, `l` "of(by?)"), གྷཱིརྟི་མ, the master's ཐོབ་ཅིག; mtsher read as 'tsher.
- Sanskrit: Sukhāvatī, Pāṇḍaravāsinī, Avalokiteśvara, Mañjuśrī, Gītā (marked perhaps), preta, kleśa, asura, Amoghasiddhi, Samayatārā, samaya, pratyavekṣaṇājñāna (note) are right.
- Known forms read against their use here: the master's entries for ཀྱིས (kyis for kyi, u. 21, 32, 36), གི, གིས ('ong gis, u. 27), གྱིས (both 'do!' and 'by'), ཅིག (u. 25), ཡང (gzhan yang, da dung yang), ཏེ, སྟེ, ཤིང, དྲུག་ཏུ (sku drug tu), ཟིན་པར (now broadened by the glosser), གྲུབ་པའི (likewise), ཐད་ཀར, ཙམ་དུ, བར་དུ, ཐོག་ཏུ, འཁྱམས, བྲོས, སྐྱེས, བསྐྱེད cover their use; only ན, བཞུགས་པ and པདྨ needed broadening (above).
- All 49 units re-read: pass 1's changes are sound; verse line counts equal in w, l, i (u. 11, 39, six lines each); the misprint notes (u. 23, 25) in the required form; u. 47's "again has no thams cad" agrees with the log (53.3, the 004 pattern).

### Findings considered and refused

- རིགས་པ (master) "rig pa as printed once with a final s": the print now has it twice (002 and u. 29 here). A broadening must keep the master entry whole, so it cannot remove "once"; the sense the entry gives is right for this use. Left for whoever edits the master.
- u. 15 · note "bskyod, past of skyod": pass 1 refused "past and future" here as no error; the sentence has the past. The gloss now gives both stems. Kept.
- u. 25 · note "cig is the print's form of zhig" against the master's ཅིག "gcig written without its prefix g-": both accounts of the indefinite cig are current; the note says "as before", following the earlier parts. Kept.
- ཤང་ཤང "in pictures part bird and part human": an iconographic remark, but the note to u. 49 (after pass 1's trim) says the same, and the word is otherwise unexplained by its letters. Kept.
- འོང་བ "'ong ba yin no 'is coming'", སྐྱེ "skye rga na 'chi …", བཞི་པ "zhag bzhi pa", དམར "dmar la": set phrases showing the form's use, as the master gives (བསུ་བ, སེར), not a line's wording. Kept.
- ལ broadening "on": the master's "at" nearly covers it, but "seated on" is the plain English of the construction and the gloss is harmless. Kept.
- ཞེན་ཅིག (master) zhen cig, where the rule gives zhig: the master gives the form without remark for 003–004 too; the print's cig for zhig/shig after n is listed in QUESTIONS.md (ཉོན་ཅིག) as a habit awaiting the owner. No broadening.
